Will County’s 54% ROI Tax Lien Secrets Exposed

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Investing in tax liens in Will County, Illinois, offers a fantastic opportunity for high returns. With an annual tax sale held every December, investors can start with an interest rate of 9% and, thanks to compounding, potentially see a 54% return over three years. Let’s break down the details for you.

Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

How They Work:

  • Tax Lien Certificates: When a property owner fails to pay their property taxes, the county sells a tax lien certificate to investors. The investor pays the outstanding taxes and earns interest on their investment.
  • Interest Rates: In Will County, the interest rate starts at 9% and can accumulate to a 54% return over three years.
  • Redemption Period: Property owners have 36 months to redeem their property by paying the back taxes plus interest. If they fail to do so, the investor can petition for a tax deed and potentially own the property.

Key Steps for Investing

Investing in tax liens in Will County involves a few essential steps to ensure you understand the process and maximize your returns.

1. Research Local Laws and Regulations

Before investing, it’s important to familiarize yourself with the laws governing tax sales in Illinois and Will County specifically. You can find up-to-date legal information on the Will County Treasurer’s Office website or by referring to the Illinois Compiled Statutes.

2. Register for the Will County Tax Lien Auction

Register for the annual tax lien sale in Will County to participate:

  • A $500 deposit is required at registration.
  • You must check in at the Will County Treasurer’s Office on the morning of the auction. Pro Tip: Register early to ensure your spot and get familiar with the auction platform.

3. Participate in the Auction

The Will County Tax Lien Auction takes place at the Will County Office Building in Joliet, IL. Here’s what you need to know:

  • Bidding Process:
    The auction uses a bid-down method, starting at 9%. The RAMS-2 system randomly selects the lowest bid among participants.
  • Location: Will County Office Building.

4. Understand What Happens After the Auction

After purchasing a tax lien certificate:

  • If the property owner redeems the lien, you’ll receive your initial investment back plus the interest earned.
  • If the lien is not redeemed within the 36-month redemption period, you can petition for a tax deed and potentially become the property’s owner.

FAQs

Can I make money from tax lien certificates?
Yes, by earning up to 9% interest per six months, you can achieve a potential return of 54% over three years.

What is a tax lien certificate?
A tax lien certificate is a legal claim on unpaid property taxes. Investors purchase these liens and earn interest on their investments.

How do I participate in the auction?
To join, you must register between October 1 and November 15, pay a $500 deposit, and attend the December auction in person.

What happens if the property owner doesn’t redeem the lien?
If the owner doesn’t redeem the lien within 36 months, you can petition for a tax deed, which may allow you to take ownership of the property.

Pro Tips for New Investors

Register Early: The sooner you sign up, the better prepared you’ll be. Register by October to ensure your spot in the auction.

Research Properties: Always research the properties before placing a bid. Some properties may have additional liens or issues.

Stay Updated: Visit the Will County Treasurer’s website regularly to stay informed about any changes or updates to the auction process.

Investing in tax liens in Will County can be a highly profitable venture if you understand the auction process and follow the guidelines. By doing your research and participating in the auction, you have the potential to earn substantial returns and even acquire property at a fraction of its market value.

Ready to Start Investing?


Visit the Will County Treasurer’s Office and register for the next auction to secure your spot and maximize your investment potential.

Investing in tax liens in Will County can be a lucrative venture if you understand the process and follow the necessary steps. Happy investing!
